newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala sees 20 pct growth in next five years.
newsitem.headline: Ayala sees 20 pct growth in next five years.

text.p: Philippine conglomerate Ayala Corp is projecting annual net income growth of 20 percent in the next five years, company president Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala said on Monday.
"I would like to keep a pace of growing at 20 percent on the average on a yearly basis, say in the period of five years," Ayala told Reuters in an interview.
He said the annual net income growth could range from 10 to 35 percent in the coming years.

The conglomerate posted a net income of 4.18 billion pesos in 1995. A recent Reuters poll of five brokerage houses said its net income could grow by 33 percent to 5.56 billion pesos in 1996. Both the 1995 figure and the forecast for 1996 exclude extraordinary gains.
"That (forecast) may be a little aggressive I think," he said, declining to give specific numbers.
But he added: "There's no doubt in my mind that very clearly we will grow significantly over last year ... Certainly, it will be comfortably over last year."
Ayala Corp has had a compounded annual growth rate of over 25 percent in the past five years.
Ayala, the Philippines oldest conglomerate, has interests in real estate, banking, insurance, telecommunications, transportation, food processing, and semiconductors.
Its units include Ayala Land, Bank of the Philippine Islands, Pure Foods Corp, Globe Telecom GMCR, Ayala Life, Insular Life and Integrated Micoelectronics Inc.
